FlightLog.title: FlightLog
FlightLog.description: Represents a single flight session of the drone, containing metadata about the entire flight.

id.description: Unique identifier for the FlightLog entity.

startTime.description: The UTC date and time when the flight officially started.

endTime.description: The UTC date and time when the flight officially ended. This can be null if the flight is still ongoing.

status.description: The current status of the flight, e.g., 'ongoing', 'completed', 'aborted', 'planned'.

description.description: An optional textual description or notes about the flight.

TelemetryPoint.title: TelemetryPoint
TelemetryPoint.description: Represents a snapshot of flight telemetry data recorded at a specific moment during a flight.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TelemetryPoint entity.

flightLogId.description: Reference to the FlightLog this telemetry point belongs to. (Relationship: FlightLog 1:N TelemetryPoint)

timestamp.description: The UTC date and time when this telemetry data was recorded.

latitude.description: The drone's current latitude in decimal degrees.

longitude.description: The drone's current longitude in decimal degrees.

altitudeMeters.description: The drone's current altitude above ground level (AGL) or sea level (ASL) in meters, as reported by the flight controller.

groundSpeedMps.description: The drone's current ground speed in meters per second.

headingDegrees.description: The drone's current heading (yaw) in degrees relative to true north (0-359).

batteryLevelPercent.description: The drone's current battery level as a percentage (0-100).

DetectionEvent.title: DetectionEvent
DetectionEvent.description: Records an instance of an object detection by the AI model during a flight.

id.description: Unique identifier for the DetectionEvent entity.

flightLogId.description: Reference to the FlightLog during which this detection occurred. (Relationship: FlightLog 1:N DetectionEvent)

timestamp.description: The UTC date and time when the object was detected.

detectedObjectType.description: The type or class of the object detected (e.g., 'camel', 'vehicle tracks').

confidenceScore.description: The confidence score of the detection, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0.

latitude.description: The drone's latitude in decimal degrees at the time of detection.

longitude.description: The drone's longitude in decimal degrees at the time of detection.

altitudeMeters.description: The drone's altitude in meters at the time of detection, derived from telemetry.

boundingBox.description: The coordinates of the bounding box around the detected object in the video frame, typically [x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max] or [x, y, width, height] as normalized or pixel values.

definition.description: Stores individual flight session logs for a specific user. This collection is owned by the 'userId' specified in the path, enabling direct authorization checks. All documents within this path are accessible only by their respective user owner.

params.description: The unique identifier for a specific flight log.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure utilizes a hierarchical, path-based ownership model to ensure strong authorization independence, clear data segregation, and efficient querying, aligning with all core design principles.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):** The design achieves authorization independence by nesting all user-specific data under a `/users/{userId}` root. Specifically, `FlightLog` documents are stored at `/users/{userId}/flightLogs/{flightLogId}`, making the `userId` (owner) explicit in the path. For subcollections like `TelemetryPoint` and `DetectionEvent`, their paths are `/users/{userId}/flightLogs/{flightLogId}/telemetryPoints/{telemetryPointId}` and `/users/{userId}/flightLogs/{flightLogId}/detectionEvents/{detectionEventId}` respectively. This structure ensures that access rules for any document in these collections can directly reference `request.auth.uid` against the `{userId}` wildcard in the path, eliminating the need for `get()` calls to parent documents (e.g., to check `FlightLog` ownership from a `TelemetryPoint` document). Furthermore, `TelemetryPoint` and `DetectionEvent` documents include the `flightLogId` field, which, while not strictly necessary for path-based authorization in this specific nested model, enhances data integrity and allows for robust rule validation (e.g., `request.resource.data.flightLogId == flightLogId`) without cross-document lookups for authorization.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** This structure inherently supports secure `list` operations (QAPs) because all documents within a given user's path are owned by that user. When a user requests a list of their `FlightLog`s, the query naturally targets `/users/{request.auth.uid}/flightLogs`. Similarly, to list `TelemetryPoint`s for a specific flight, the query targets `/users/{request.auth.uid}/flightLogs/{flightLogId}/telemetryPoints`. Firestore security rules can directly validate `request.auth.uid == userId` for the parent collection, and then apply additional checks (e.g., `flightLogId` equality in subcollection documents) without filtering sensitive data. Each collection (`flightLogs`, `telemetryPoints`, `detectionEvents`) maintains a homogeneous security posture (all documents owned by the `userId` in the path), simplifying rules and preventing accidental data exposure.
